background.task:
The bot stealth evaluation is complete. The report is at `target/bot-stealth-report.md`. Key findings:

- **Browser4 successfully evades the most critical check:** `navigator.webdriver` is `false` across all 5 services
- **2 of 5 services gave a clean PASS** (Sannysoft, BrowserScan)
- **3 of 5 services flagged Browser4** for non-automation issues: `hardwareConcurrency` leakage in Web Workers, WebGL shader inconsistency, datacenter IP, and timezone mismatch
- **Google search was blocked** — Google served a CAPTCHA, preventing Phase 1 of the task

issues.title: Google CAPTCHA blocks browser4-cli — bot detected at network level

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 goto "https://www.google.com/search?q=online+bot+detection+test" — redirected to google.com/sorry CAPTCHA page.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Google search results page loads normally.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Redirected to https://www.google.com/sorry/index?... CAPTCHA challenge page blocking the search.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Google's bot detection combines IP reputation (datacenter IP: 133.18.123.58, KAGOYA JAPAN Inc.) with browser fingerprint signals. While navigator.webdriver is false, Google uses additional signals — likely WebGL fingerprinting, canvas fingerprinting, IP reputation, and hardwareConcurrency inconsistency between main thread and Web Workers.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Ensure navigator.hardwareConcurrency is consistently overridden across the main thread AND Web Workers
- Add support for configuring proxy/network settings to route through residential IPs
- Investigate what specific signals Google uses beyond navigator.webdriver to detect Browser4
- Consider implementing Google-specific stealth patches (e.g., overriding the Google-specific bot detection APIs)
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: fill --submit does not submit the form on Google (no navigation occurs)

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 goto "https://www.google.com"; ./b4w.ps1 fill <searchbox-ref> "search query" --submit — fills text but URL stays at google.com, no navigation.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Text is filled and form is submitted (Enter pressed), navigating to search results.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Text fills successfully and command reports success, but the page URL remains https://www.google.com/ — no navigation occurs.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The --submit flag may only work for <form> elements with standard submit actions. Google's search page uses JavaScript-based form handling that doesn't respond to a traditional Enter/submit. Alternatively, --submit might send Enter to the wrong element or rely on form.submit() which JS-heavy pages intercept.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: CLI: cli/browser4-cli/src/ — fill command handler; Backend: browser4-rest/ — fill tool executor
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- After fill + Enter, verify the page URL changed; if not, explicitly call press Enter on the input element
- Document the --submit flag's behavior clearly: what exactly it does (press Enter vs form.submit())
- Add a --submit-selector option to target a specific submit button to click
- For Google specifically, fill + press Enter should work — document as a known pattern
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: fill command timed out after failed fill --submit

sections.body: After a fill --submit that doesn't navigate (see Issue 2), run ./b4w.ps1 fill <ref> "text" — the command times out after 30s.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Second fill completes quickly by filling text into the field.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The fill command timed out (30s) and was moved to background. Page appears to be in an inconsistent state after the first incomplete submit.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: After fill --submit, Google's JS may still be processing the incomplete submit, leaving the element in an unfocusable or locked state. The fill command waits for the element to become interactable and hangs indefinitely.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Add a timeout parameter for fill operations with a sensible default (5-10s)
- Detect and recover from stuck page states after failed operations
- Provide a clear error message when an element is not interactable, rather than hanging
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Session lost after tab operations — requires manual reconnection

sections.body: Run tab-new, then tab-select, then any interaction command. Error: "No active session is currently stored for this CLI context."
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Session persists across tab operations; commands work without reconnection.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: After tab-new and tab-select, the session context was lost. Had to re-run goto to reconnect. Error message requires understanding of CLI session management.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Tab operations may not properly persist or update the CLI-side session tracking. When tab-switching occurs, the CLI's session reference may become stale or not be updated to track the new active tab.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: CLI: cli/browser4-cli/src/ — session management module
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Ensure tab operations (tab-new, tab-select) update the CLI session state
- Auto-reconnect session transparently if session context is lost
- Provide a clearer diagnostic: "Session lost. Run goto <url> or open to reconnect."
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: tab-list shows stale/incorrect URLs after navigation

sections.body: After tab-new to google.com and navigation, eval shows actual URL is localhost:18080 but tab-list still shows https://www.google.com.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: tab-list displays the actual current URL of each tab as reported by the browser.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: tab-list showed https://www.google.com for a tab that was actually displaying a mock ecommerce page at localhost:18080.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Tab URL tracking in the CLI may be based on the last navigation command rather than polling actual browser state. When a page redirects or browser internal navigation changes, tab-list may not reflect the actual URL.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: CLI: tab-list command implementation
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- tab-list should query the browser for actual current URLs, not rely on cached navigation history
- Add a --refresh flag to force polling actual browser state
- Display a warning indicator when a tab URL may be stale
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: htmlsnapshot export argument syntax unclear — produces error

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot export ".test-sessions/results.html" — error: "too many arguments: expected 0, received 1"
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Command accepts a file path and exports snapshot there, OR help text clearly explains where export goes without arguments.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Help says "Export snapshot HTML to a local file" but rejects any path argument. Export destination is unknown. User must guess or read source code.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The command likely exports to a fixed location (snapshot directory) but the help text says 'to a local file' implying user control. The argument parser rejects any arguments.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: CLI: htmlsnapshot export command definition
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Accept a file path argument: htmlsnapshot export [path]
- Or update help text to show the export path: "Export to <snapshot-dir>/export-<timestamp>.html"
- Show the export destination path in command output after successful export
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Page context becomes stale after htmlsnapshot — eval returns empty

sections.body: goto <url> → htmlsnapshot → eval "document.body.innerText" returns "Eval returned empty/null. The page context may be stale."
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: eval works after htmlsnapshot to extract live page data. The natural workflow is goto → htmlsnapshot → eval/extract.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: After capturing HTML snapshot, eval on the live page returns empty/null. Required re-running goto before eval could work again.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: htmlsnapshot appears to take a static snapshot and may disconnect from the live page context, or there's a session tracking issue where the live page reference is lost after snapshotting.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: Backend: browser4-rest/ — htmlsnapshot controller; session tracking
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- htmlsnapshot should not affect the live page/session reference
- If it must disconnect, document this clearly in help and SKILL.md
- Provide a --keep-context flag to preserve the live page reference
- Auto-reconnect the live page context when eval detects staleness
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: hardwareConcurrency leaks real value through Web Workers — detected by 3 of 5 services

sections.body: Visit incolumitas.com or deviceandbrowserinfo.com with Browser4. Both detect hasInconsistentWorkerValues: true because hardwareConcurrency is 4 in main thread but 20 in Web Workers.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: If hardwareConcurrency is overridden on the main thread, the same override applies in Web Workers.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Override only applies on the main thread. Web Workers expose the real hardwareConcurrency value (20), creating a detectable inconsistency.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Browser4 likely patches navigator.hardwareConcurrency via CDP's Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument which only affects the main document context, not Web Worker contexts which have their own isolated JS environment.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-core/browser4-browser/ — PulsarWebDriver stealth/evasion patches
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Extend navigator.hardwareConcurrency override to Web Worker contexts
- Alternatively, use a kernel-level or browser-level override that affects all contexts
- Add a test case specifically for Web Worker navigator consistency
- Document this as a known limitation if it cannot be fixed
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: No --full-page option for screenshot — cannot capture long result pages

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 screenshot on a long result page — only captures the visible viewport. Content below the fold is not included.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Option to capture full-page screenshot (entire scrollable content), or at minimum a --full-page flag.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Only viewport screenshots available. Long result pages (like incolumitas.com) cannot be fully captured in one image.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: screenshot uses CDP's Page.captureScreenshot with default viewport clipping. Full-page screenshots require the captureBeyondViewport or fullPage parameter.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: Backend: browser4-core/browser4-browser/ — PulsarWebDriver screenshot implementation
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Add --full-page flag to screenshot for full-page capture
- Add --clip option to capture specific regions
- Document the viewport-only limitation in help and SKILL.md
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
